note.μέλητος: Meletus, who brought the formal indictment. Socrates cross-examines him at 24c–28a.
note.ἄνυτος: Anytus, a prominent politician and the weightiest of the three accusers; he appears for the craftsmen and politicians (23e–24a).
note.λύκων: Lycon, the third accuser, appearing on behalf of the orators (23e–24a).
note.σωκράτης: Socrates, speaking in his own defence before an Athenian jury in 399 BC.
note.ἀθηναῖος: Athenian. Socrates addresses the jury throughout as ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, ‘men of Athens’.
note.χαιρεφῶν: Chaerephon, Socrates' friend, who asked the Delphic oracle whether anyone was wiser than Socrates (21a).
note.κρίτων: Crito, Socrates' lifelong friend and fellow-demesman, present at the trial (33d) and among those offering to guarantee the fine (38b).
note.κριτόβουλος: Critobulus, son of Crito, named among those present (33e).
note.πρόδικος: Prodicus of Ceos, a sophist named alongside Gorgias and Hippias (19e).
note.ἱππίας: Hippias of Elis, a sophist named alongside Gorgias and Prodicus (19e).
note.εὔηνος: Evenus of Paros, who taught for a fee of five minae (20b).
note.ἀριστοφάνης: Aristophanes, the comic poet; Socrates points to his portrayal in the Clouds (19c).
note.παλαμήδης: Palamedes, condemned unjustly by the Greeks at Troy; one of the dead Socrates imagines meeting (41b).
note.αἰακός: Aeacus, one of the judges of the dead, named with Minos, Rhadamanthus and Triptolemus (41a).
note.ὀρφεύς: Orpheus, named among the dead Socrates would gladly meet (41a).
note.μουσαῖος: Musaeus, a legendary poet named with Orpheus and Hesiod (41a).
note.ἡσίοδος: Hesiod, named among the poets Socrates would question in the underworld (41a).
note.ὅμηρος: Homer, named among the poets Socrates would question in the underworld (41a).
note.θέτις: Thetis, mother of Achilles, whose warning Socrates quotes from the Iliad (28c).
note.τριπτόλεμος: Triptolemus, named among the judges of the dead (41a).
note.δίη: Here the form Δία is the accusative of Ζεύς, in the oaths μὰ Δία and νὴ Δία, ‘by Zeus’. The parser also offers Δίη, a place name, which is not what Plato means.
note.αἰσχίνης: Aeschines, one of Socrates' companions present at the trial (33e).
note.δημόδοκος: Demodocus, father of Theages, named at 33e.
note.θεάγης: Theages, brother of Paralus, named among those present (33e).
note.ἀντιφῶν: Antiphon of Cephisia, father of Epigenes, named at 33e.
note.ἀδείμαντος: Adeimantus, Plato's brother, named among those present (34a).
note.ἀπολλόδωρος: Apollodorus, a devoted follower of Socrates, named at 34a.
note.πλάτων: Plato, named by Socrates as present at the trial (34a) — one of the few places he names himself.
note.θεόδοτος: Theodotus, named among those present, already dead at the time of the trial (33e).
note.νικόστρατος: Nicostratus, brother of Theodotus, named at 33e.
note.ἐπιγένης: Epigenes, son of Antiphon, named at 33e.
note.λεοντῖνος: Of Leontini, in Sicily — the home of Gorgias.
note.κεῖος: Of Ceos, the island home of Prodicus.
note.κλαζομένιος: Of Clazomenae, in Ionia — the home of Anaxagoras.
note.πάριος: Of Paros, the island home of Evenus.
note.ἠλεῖος: Of Elis, in the Peloponnese — the home of Hippias.
note.δελφοί: Delphi, seat of the oracle of Apollo, which Chaerephon consulted (21a).
note.πύθιος: Pythian, of Delphi — an epithet of Apollo.
note.πρυτανεῖον: The Prytaneum, where Athens entertained its public benefactors at state expense — the ‘penalty’ Socrates proposes for himself (36d).
note.σαλαμίς: Salamis, from which Socrates was ordered to arrest Leon under the Thirty (32c).
note.λέων: Leon of Salamis, whom Socrates refused to arrest for the Thirty (32c).
note.γοργίης: Gorgias of Leontini, the celebrated teacher of rhetoric, named among the travelling sophists (19e).
note.καλλίης: Callias, a wealthy Athenian who spent heavily on sophists for his sons (20a).
note.λυσανίης: Lysanias of Sphettus, father of Aeschines (33e).
note.ἀναξαγόρης: Anaxagoras of Clazomenae, the natural philosopher whose views Meletus attributes to Socrates (26d).
note.ἀρίστων: Ariston, father of Plato and Adeimantus (34a).
